economy.summary: Supports an immediate increase in the minimum wage, calling Pennsylvania's $7.25 rate unchanged since 2009 not livable, and backs policies to keep costs of living low.
economy.short: Supports minimum wage increase and keeping costs of living low.

taxes.summary: Calls for significant tax reform so that district taxpayers benefit from their contributions, and says local tax revenue should return to benefit district infrastructure and services.
taxes.short: Supports tax reform returning taxpayer contributions to the district.

abortion.summary: Says the majority of Pennsylvania supports a woman's right to autonomy over her own body, and defends reproductive decisions made between patients and their doctors.
abortion.short: Supports reproductive autonomy; defends patient-doctor reproductive decisions.

education.summary: Supports raising teacher pay, equitable school funding, and removing barriers to educational access, saying strong schools require effective resourcing and teacher support.
education.short: Supports raising teacher pay and equitable school funding.

healthcare.summary: Says individuals deserve access to affordable and equitable healthcare; proposes lowering premiums and holding insurance and pharmaceutical companies accountable.
healthcare.short: Supports affordable healthcare; would hold insurers and drugmakers accountable.

energy.summary: Supports policies protecting clean air and water while enabling economic growth and expansion of green energy without environmental harm.
energy.short: Supports clean air and water protections plus green energy expansion.

guns.summary: His platform's community safety section proposes directing tax dollars toward community healthcare, public health outreach, and well-resourced schools and emergency services; it does not state positions on firearms.
guns.short: Community-safety plan funds local services; no stated firearms positions.

economy.summary: Co-authored House Bill 1108, which would let lower-income working parents who get a raise keep their child care subsidy at a higher copay for the rest of the benefit year, saying the bill smooths the child care cliff so parents can accept a raise and keep essential child care.
economy.short: Co-authored bill letting working parents keep child care subsidies.

taxes.summary: Opposed Governor Shapiro's 2026-27 budget proposal, saying it spends $6.4 billion more than the state has, and warned that draining the Rainy Day Fund could lead to a large tax increase on working families; says the state must tighten its belt now to avoid cuts or tax increases later.
taxes.short: Opposes Shapiro budget; warns it risks tax increases on families.

abortion.summary: In July 2022 voted for Senate Bill 106, a joint resolution proposing constitutional amendments including one providing there is no constitutional right to taxpayer-funded abortion or any other right relating to abortion.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment stating constitution grants no abortion right.

education.summary: Proposed a Pennsylvania College Voucher Program that would redirect about $580 million in state funding for Pitt, Penn State, and Temple into direct yearly grants of up to $8,000 for students at technical schools, community colleges, and other institutions, saying it would empower students seeking more affordable education options.
education.short: Proposes redirecting state university funding into direct student grants.

energy.summary: One of the sponsors of a 2026 House Republican energy package aimed at lowering electricity costs and expanding in-state power generation, saying more power equals lower prices and that the most affordable energy is power produced in Pennsylvania.
energy.short: Sponsors energy package; says more power equals lower prices.

guns.summary: In November 2021 voted for Senate Bill 565, which would have removed the requirement to obtain a license to carry a concealed firearm in Pennsylvania.
guns.short: Voted to remove license requirement for concealed carry.
